what: Persistent contact (option 4, D0016 approved Nov 11) built on method/persistent-contact, worktree sequel-data/worktrees/persistent-contact. Tests run with the branch engine on PYTHONPATH and the main venv, 2026-11-11.
identity_with_main: method off (v_sleep 0): bit-identical S, W, counters and energy terms to main at the end of each of 50 cycles at 3 2D conditions (Gamma 3.5: f* 0.3 depth 5, f* 0.5 depth 5, f* 0.3 depth 10; L 50, seed 1)
v2_tests: rest, ride (z = z_p + h, v = v_p to 1e-12) and release at sin(om t) = 1/Gamma against the closed form
fast landing bounces; no rest while g_eff < 0; none with the method off
a sphere dropped on a Gamma 0.5 plate ends at rest after finitely many (10 to 50000) plate collisions
energy and momentum residuals below 1e-8 every cycle with sleeps, releases, slow and fast hits (2D, Gamma 2.2, v_sleep 3e-2)
v3_tests: two-sphere stack rests, rides and releases together (closed form)
pressed oblique pair at offsets 0.35 and 0.6 rests on its first hit; the steeper one is counted as a rest steeper than the friction angle
fast hit on the bottom of a three-sphere chain wakes the two above (cascade)
slow hit equals the plate collision operator along the line of centres
energy and momentum balance below 1e-8 with piles: up to 37 spheres resting on spheres at once in 15 cycles (2D, N 150, Gamma 2.2, v_sleep 3e-2, v_wakeup 6e-2)
known_limitation_strict_xfail: a sphere bounced off a resting one at 2e-3 rolls off at about 0.08 and stalls rolling on a Gamma 0.5 plate: the approved rule needs the full speed relative to the plate below v_sleep (D0020)
